summary: Health systems are deploying clinical artificial intelligence (AI) faster than they can govern it, and existing frameworks emphasize risk oversight over operational learning and scale. The Collaborative Technology Adoption for Care Transformation (C-TACT) framework, developed at Southern California Permanente Medical Group (SCPMG), organizes governance across three pillars (People, Process, Technology) and four lifecycle stages (Vendor Evaluation, Pilot, Scale, Maintenance), each operationalized through a domain-weighted scorecard. Scale and Maintenance scorecards incorporate business and operational execution as weighted domains, with Analytic Hierarchy Process methods (consistency ratio 0.0037). In an illustrative, retrospective application, the Pilot Score Card separated two published SCPMG AI deployments and four anonymized comparators (47.0–53.5) by approximately thirty points across three weighting schemes. This separation illustrates how the framework behaves in this comparison. It is not evidence of validated discriminative performance, because the comparator scores were reconstructed retrospectively and were not scored under blinded conditions. C-TACT is presented here as a governance framework and a methodological demonstration. Prospective, blinded validation is needed to establish its discriminative and predictive performance under real-world conditions.
title: Clinical AI governance for scalable innovation in value based healthcare systems

summary: The electronic health record (EHR) comprises structured and unstructured data, both of which are integral for comprehensively representing patient history. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has enabled the incorporation of unstructured data modalities into machine learning models that leverage EHR data. In this systematic review, we characterize studies that utilize LLM-enabled multimodal predictive modeling with EHR data. Following a screening of 641 studies, 57 met inclusion criteria. We identified three strategies for LLM-based multimodal integration: embedding, extraction, and text fusion. Delineated by the format of the unstructured data at the time of fusion, all strategies yielded performance gains (average 6.4% increase) over single modality models. LLMs facilitated modeling by generating note-embeddings for downstream prediction, extracting clinically informative variables, and summarizing long text documents prior to integration. Building on our review, we identified LLM-enhanced predictive modeling considerations that include sample size, interpretability, and computational costs. This study supports the potential value of LLMs for EHR-based predictive modeling and provides a framework for future multimodal modeling tools.
title: Large language models for multimodal clinical predictive modeling: a systematic review

summary: Osteoporosis (OP) and neurodegeneration frequently co-occur with advancing age, but the biological processes linking skeletal and neurological decline remain incompletely understood. To investigate the metabolic-inflammatory axis connecting skeletal and neurological degeneration, we integrated cross-tissue multi-omics, single-cell transcriptomics, in vitro macrophage assays, and systems-level ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based modeling. Population-level and genetically informed analyses consistently implicated metabolic burden and lipid-associated stress in both disease domains, whereas physical activity showed protective associations. Cross-tissue and single-cell analyses identified convergent autophagy- and inflammasome-related programs, while cross-tissue multi-omics highlighted a PHF23-MCL1-CLN3 autophagy-associated molecular module. In RAW264.7 macrophages, oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL) exposure induced inflammatory activation, pro-inflammatory polarization, and autophagy-associated dysregulation, while PHF23 perturbation modified ox-LDL-induced inflammatory responses. A 12-state ODE model further provided a hypothesis-generating representation of dynamic interactions among ox-LDL-associated metabolic stress, autophagy regulation, inflammasome activation, macrophage polarization, and tissue-damage-related states. Together, these multi-scale findings provide convergent support for an ox-LDL-autophagy-inflammasome-associated framework linking metabolic dysfunction with skeletal and neurological degeneration and generate testable hypotheses for further experimental investigation.
title: Multi-scale integration identifies an ox-LDL-autophagy-inflammasome framework linking osteoporosis and neurodegeneration

summary: Turner Syndrome (TS) is a chromosomal disorder characterized by growth retardation and congenital ovarian dysgenesis. Given the considerable morbidity and mortality, early diagnosis and timely intervention are crucial to improving outcomes. However, the gold standard diagnostic method, karyotype analysis, is time-consuming and requires specialized laboratory expertise. Since TS patients often present distinct facial features, AI-based facial recognition could help identify patients with characteristic appearance as a screening tool. Inspired by the value-of-information principle, we propose a hybrid framework integrating deep feature learning and geometric prior knowledge under data scarcity. We retrospectively constructed this AI facial recognition model for TS detection and validated it in a prospective cohort. The proposed framework achieved 95.41% accuracy, 96.55% sensitivity, and 95.24% specificity, substantially simplifying the diagnostic process. When training was performed only on the hard subset obtained after difficulty-based stratification into three equal groups, the sensitivity reached 100.00%, indicating that all patients were correctly identified. Grad-CAM visualization of key facial regions improved model interpretability and aligned predictions with clinical insights. Our method offers a low-cost and easily accessible approach to TS screening. By allowing for an earlier detection of TS, particularly in medical resource-limited settings, this method has the potential to facilitate timely interventions. This novel paradigm also provides insight for facial recognition-aided diagnosis in other diseases.
title: A hybrid framework for Turner Syndrome facial detection: integrating deep feature learning and geometric prior knowledge under data scarcity

summary: Evaluation of AI-generated patient communication lacks standardized frameworks, and automated metrics may not reflect clinical utility. We leveraged a staged rollout of GPT-generated draft responses (GDRs) to patient portal messages. Thirty primary care physicians received drafts from September 2023 to August 2024 under two conditions: an intervention group where AI drafts were displayed and edited (n = 21,073), and a non-displayed group where drafts were generated but never shown to physicians, who composed responses independently (n = 45,127). We evaluated messages using BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, and Flesch Reading Ease, and then correlated automated metrics with blinded physician ratings of effectiveness, misunderstanding potential, and harm. In the intervention group, 2264 (11%) drafts were incorporated into final messages with high semantic alignment (BERTScore F1 = 0.93). In the non-displayed group, independent physician messages showed moderate similarity to unseen drafts (BERTScore F1 = 0.83). Despite comparable semantic scores, physicians preferred human-authored messages (4.24/5). BERTScore correlated with physician quality ratings in the intervention group but not in the non-displayed. Automated metrics demonstrated context-dependent validity; they assessed editing fidelity but failed to evaluate whether AI-generated content matches independent human performance. Rigorous evaluation of clinical generative AI requires validation of metric meaning within specific use contexts.
title: Silent evaluation reveals context-dependent validity of automated metrics for AI-generated clinical messages

summary: The reliability of emergent histopathology foundation models (Histo-FMs) for real-world diagnostic tasks remains unproven. Given the complexity of diagnostic tasks and the challenges inherent in real-world data, we utilized Histo-FMs to investigate their utility for morphological subtyping of Barrett’s esophagus (BE) and detecting esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) across the BE progression spectrum. We benchmarked Histo-FMs on the BarrettNet cohort, spanning diagnostic categories ranging from normal to EAC (N2EAC). The dataset comprised 3528 hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) from 790 patients. A multi-magnification, multi-backbone aggregation of the five most expert-consistent single-scale models yielded incremental performance gains (AUROC of 0.907, F1-score of 0.696, accuracy of 0.795, and κ of 0.651 for morphological subtyping; AUROC of 0.909, F1-score of 0.836, accuracy of 0.959, and κ of 0.673 for EAC detection), with non-uniform gains across single-model comparisons and limited benefit for dysplasia. The findings support the capability of Histo-FMs for BE morphological subtyping and EAC detection in a multicenter clinical cohort, while highlighting persistent challenges in dysplasia assessment and the need for external validation. This study provides a foundation for future clinical validation.
title: Towards reliable morphological subtyping and cancer detection on Barrett’s esophagus pathology through ensembling foundation models

summary: Lung puncture biopsy is the gold standard for the qualitative diagnosis of lung nodules. Cone Beam CT (CBCT) is commonly used for guiding punctures to locate lung nodules. However, the poor quality of CBCT images and the limited intelligence of surgical guidance systems have lowered the efficiency of puncture procedures, particularly for small and complex lesions. This study developed and validated a robust and accurate Generative AI-Powered Puncture Surgery Navigation System for lung punctures (GPS-Lung), demonstrating clinical applicability through a multicenter randomized controlled trial (Registration number: NCT06762613). The clinical results showed significant improvements in surgeon performance with the assistance of the integrated GPS-Lung system. Specifically, the system facilitated a more standardized and efficient operational process, reducing number of punctures (2.0 ± 1.2 vs. 2.5 ± 1.7, P = 0.005), shortening operative time (20.4 ± 5.6 min vs. 23.2 ± 6.3 min, P = 0.001), decreasing radiation exposure (4357.4 ± 3427.3 μGy·m2 vs. 5570.9 ± 4846.7 μGy·m2, P = 0.033), and reducing pneumothorax complications (12.7% vs. 23.9%, P = 0.033). Taken together, the proposed system demonstrates promising clinical and translational value in lung nodule puncture intervention. (Clinical Trials Registration: NCT06762613). Clinical Trials Registration: NCT06762613, Registration Date: March 26, 2025. (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06762613?term=NCT06762613&rank=1&tab=history).
title: A Generative AI-powered navigation system for precision CBCT-guided lung biopsies: a randomized controlled trial

summary: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a leading cause of cardiovascular mortality, yet the real-world performance of FDA-cleared AI detection models remains incompletely characterized. We retrospectively evaluated two FDA-cleared AI algorithms from a single commercial platform (Aidoc Medical BriefCase)—one for PE triage on dedicated CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA; n = 30,678) and one for incidental PE (iPE) detection on routine contrast-enhanced CTs (n = 37,191), across a 17-facility academic health system. Reference-standard labels were extracted from radiology reports using a validated LLM pipeline (97% accuracy, κ = 0.94). The PE model achieved 86.8% sensitivity and 99.1% specificity, with sensitivity declining from 99.3% for saddle emboli to 72.9% for subsegmental PE, and from 89.7% for acute to 65.3% for non-acute PE. The iPE model achieved 73.5% sensitivity and 99.8% specificity. Both models demonstrated lower sensitivity than FDA-clearance benchmarks while exceeding cleared specificity, with diminishing performance for peripheral and non-acute emboli mirroring known human reader limitations and underscoring the need for standardized post-market surveillance of AI-enabled medical devices.
title: Multi-site real-world performance of commercial AI for pulmonary and incidental pulmonary embolism detection
